title: When: The Scientific Secrets of Perfect Timing
author: Daniel H. Pink
target_audience: General readers interested in science-based self-improvement
Business professionals and managers seeking to optimize productivity
Students and educators exploring cognitive performance
Readers interested in behavioral science and decision-making
core_themes: The science of timing and its impact on decision-making
The importance of breaks and rest for performance and creativity
Optimal timing for key life and business events
Using timing science to enhance motivation and well-being
primary_purpose: To reveal how scientific research on timing can help people make better decisions and optimize outcomes in work, health, learning, and personal life by understanding and harnessing natural rhythms and best moments to act.

structure_format.organization: Structured around key questions of 'when' to act, divided into sections on daily timing, beginnings, middles, endings, and group timing
features: Digestible summaries and practical takeaways ('Time Hacker’s Handbook' at each chapter’s end)
Discussion of scientific studies from psychology, biology, and economics

key_concepts_lessons: Human performance and mood rise and fall in predictable daily patterns (chronotypes, circadian rhythms).
There are optimal times for different types of work; analytical tasks are best done in the morning, insight-oriented tasks later.
Taking breaks—especially social, outside, and movement-based—is essential for sustained performance.
Beginnings, middles, and endings each shape behavior differently—how you start, the midpoint’s 'slump' or 'spark,' and the finish line’s motivational boost.
Strategically timing events (meetings, exams, changes) can yield better outcomes.
Understanding your own biological rhythms can enhance personal productivity and happiness.
notable_features: Practical tips grounded in behavioral science
'Time Hacker’s Handbook' summaries for real-world application
Stories from business, education, medicine, and sports
Focus on timing as a neglected yet crucial factor for success
cultural_historical_context: Published in the late 2010s amid a wave of bestsellers on behavioral science and productivity, the book draws on advances in psychology, chronobiology, and economics to highlight timing’s emerging role in decision-making research and personal optimization.
reception_impact: Well-received bestseller with praise for its practical and actionable insights
Appreciated for making scientific findings relatable and usable for everyday decisions
Used in business, education, coaching, and healthcare contexts
Critics note a reliance on anecdotal as well as scientific evidence
comparable_titles: Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us by Daniel H. Pink
The Power of When by Michael Breus
Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise by Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool
